root.name: Petrov's Defense: French Attack
root.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nf6 3. Nxe5 d6 4. Nf3 Nxe4 5. d3

overview: White hits the e4 knight with 5.d3 instead of the main 5.d4. Black retreats 5...Nf6 and White continues with 6.d4 d5, reaching a symmetrical Petrov position, or plays Be2 and O-O with a slower set-up. Both sides develop quietly and the structure stays symmetrical with an open e-file; the game is steady and rarely tactical early. White hopes for a small initiative, Black for easy equality.

white_ideas.idea: Gain a tempo on the knight and go 6.d4 d5 with a safe symmetrical position
Develop Be2, O-O, Nc3 and use the open e-file
Keep options of Bg5 or Nbd2 to avoid the main-line symmetry

black_ideas.idea: Retreat ...Nf6 and play ...d5 for a symmetrical structure
Challenge e4 or d4 pawns only if White errs

typical_structures.structure: Symmetrical pawns on a-b-c-d-f-g-h with the e-file open

character.notes: Symmetrical, steady and hard for White to crack. Solid.

structure.notes: Symmetrical exchange structure with an open e-file; Semi-open per taxonomy.

approach.notes: A respectable variation within the Petrov; standard.

level.notes: Easy to play but little to learn; Intermediate. Could be Beginner for a quiet repertoire, but Black's plans take some judgement.

sublines_that_differ.name: 5...Nf6 6.d4 d5
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nf6 3. Nxe5 d6 4. Nf3 Nxe4 5. d3 Nf6 6. d4 d5
sublines_that_differ.how: The main continuation, transposing to a symmetrical Petrov.

character.reason: Symmetrical, low-risk play where Black is very hard to break down.

structure.reason: The taxonomy places symmetrical Petrov structures with an open e-file here.

approach.reason: A mainstream, if less common, White option against the Petrov.

level.reason: Easy to play but requires understanding of the Petrov's early traps.

plans.reason: Both sides have mirror-image pawns and play for small edges.
